## At a glance {#td-sheet}

```{=html}
<p class="td-note">Everything in one table: every tune, classical theme, piece (including those known only from a print anthology), Words &amp; Chords song, Billboard song, score, and MLT / JRI recording not linked to a tune. The <b>type buttons</b> switch types on and off.
<b>Clicking:</b> a title opens the piece where it lives on this site (Tune Library, Classical Themes, Words &amp; Chords, the full-score player, Timestamp Notes, the Recordings Catalogue), in this tab; a title with no page of its own opens its details here. ▸ opens a row's details (every recording, playable, the places it is used, where it came from); ⏱ opens its first recording in Timestamp Notes. Links off the site open in a new tab and are marked ↗.
<b>Group movements</b> puts the movements, themes and scores of one big piece (same composer and catalogue number, e.g. K. 550) under one row; ▸ opens it. <b>Columns</b> chooses which columns show (remembered).
<b>Concepts</b> counts the places where a teaching source (Hutchinson's textbook and others) uses the piece to show a concept; pick a concept (grouped by source) or a source above the table. <b>Year</b> is the year of composition (or publication); <b>Print</b> the anthology figure. Type in the
box under a column to filter it (in Recordings and Bars marked: <code>&gt;0</code>, <code>0</code>, <code>2</code>); click a column name
to sort. <b>Bars marked</b> counts recordings with a timing map. The sections below are the same
collections, grouped; they start folded (click a heading to open one). They still hold what the table cannot: the anthology figures by composer, the music finder's results (Functions, Progression, tonal pattern…) and the analysed scores.</p>
<div id="td-sheet-box"></div>
```

## Pieces with recordings and resources {#td-works}

```{=html}
<p class="td-note"><span id="td-works-n"></span>. A piece groups every place it appears on the site (a tune in several keys, a

<div id="td-works-list"></div>
```

## Print anthologies {#td-print}
```{=html}
<p class="td-note"><span id="td-print-n"></span> from the analysis anthologies used in class, by the book's figure number
(chapter–figure; ★ a complete movement), with the year of composition where Wikidata or the theme data has it. Most have no
notation or recording here yet; a <b>theme</b> link opens the same piece on the Classical Themes page. The concepts each figure shows
are in the <a href="../course/glossary.html">glossary</a>.</p>
<div id="td-print-list"></div>
```

## Billboard songs (chords and form) {#td-billboard}

```{=html}
<p class="td-note"><span id="td-bb-n"></span> from the McGill Billboard Project (1958–1991): each song's sections, bars and chords,
timed. A title opens it in <a href="../tools/timestamp-notes.html">Timestamp Notes</a>; no recording comes with it, so find the song on
YouTube and paste the link there.</p>
<div id="td-billboard-list"></div>
```

## Beatles songs (chords and form, Isophonics) {#td-isophonics}

```{=html}
<p class="td-note"><span id="td-iso-n"></span> from the Isophonics Beatles annotations (Queen Mary, University of London): every chord, by beat, with sections and keys. The bars come from the annotators' beat files, so a bar may be a
beat or two out where the beat tracking was; the time signature is read from the beat count, not annotated. A title opens it in
<a href="../tools/timestamp-notes.html">Timestamp Notes</a>, like a Billboard song.</p>
<div id="td-isophonics-list"></div>
```

## Works Cited

<!-- works-cited: written by scripts/works-cited.py -->
::: {.works-cited}
Burgoyne, John Ashley, Jonathan Wild, and Ichiro Fujinaga. "An Expert Ground Truth Set for Audio Chord Recognition and Music Analysis." *Proceedings of the 12th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference*, Miami, 2011, pp. 633–38. The 890 SALAMI chords files of the McGill Billboard Project (songs from the Billboard Hot 100, 1958–1991): sections, bars and chords, timed; released under CC0. [ddmal.ca/research/The_McGill_Billboard_Project_(Chord_Analysis_Dataset)/](https://ddmal.ca/research/The_McGill_Billboard_Project_(Chord_Analysis_Dataset)/).

Isophonics. Centre for Digital Music, Queen Mary, University of London, isophonics.net. Beatles chord, key, beat and segment annotations, personal and educational use. [isophonics.net/](http://isophonics.net/).

**For students**

12tone. "I Listened To 500 Songs To Prove A Point." *YouTube*, [www.youtube.com/watch?v=F7be6Aicdo0](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F7be6Aicdo0). Loop shape (contour, anchoring), chord functions, loop types and the survey numbers; read from the transcript.

Hein, Ethan. "Pieces vs Songs vs Grooves." *Ethan Teaches You Music*, Substack, 6 June 2021, [ethanhein.substack.com/p/pieces-vs-songs-vs-grooves](https://ethanhein.substack.com/p/pieces-vs-songs-vs-grooves). Definitions, examples by category and the claims about notation and music education.

Hein, Ethan. "Songs vs Grooves." *Ethan Teaches You Music Podcast*, Substack, 3 June 2026, [ethanhein.substack.com/p/songs-vs-grooves-59a](https://ethanhein.substack.com/p/songs-vs-grooves-59a). Track list only; the audio was not heard.

**For teachers**

Cutler, Timothy. *Anthology of Music for Analysis*. W. W. Norton, 2019. Its Index of Composers and Works and Index of Concepts: the figure numbers in the Tune Directory and the examples under glossary terms.

Hein, Ethan. "Blues Tonality." *The Ethan Hein Blog*, 21 Sept. 2014, updated 10 Jan. 2026, [www.ethanhein.com/wp/2014/blues-tonality/](https://www.ethanhein.com/wp/2014/blues-tonality/). The series' main source; its own reference list has the books and articles named on these pages.

Tagg, Philip. *Everyday Tonality II: Towards a Tonal Theory of What Most People Hear*. The Mass Media Music Scholars' Press, 2014. E-book version 2.5.2. The pieces in its index, with pages, are in the Tune Directory.

Wikidata. Wikimedia Foundation. [www.wikidata.org/](https://www.wikidata.org/). Years of composition (inception) or publication of the pieces, matched by composer and catalogue number; CC0.
:::
